title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
technique: KV cache eviction keeping a balance of recent tokens and 'heavy hitter' tokens ranked by accumulated attention score; fixed KV budget (e.g. 20%)

optimized_metrics.evidence: we introduce a novel approach for implementing the KV cache which significantly reduces its memory footprint.
an ideal KV cache should have (i) a small cache size to reduce memory footprint, (ii) a low miss rate to maintain the performance and long-content generation ability of LLMs
we implement H2O on top of FlexGen that can easily adapt different cache eviction techniques to produce a system with high-throughput inference
We provide a general framework that can support any KV cache eviction algorithm and enhance throughput and reduce the latency of LLM generation with careful implementation.

headline_claim.text: H2O with 20% heavy hitters improves the throughput over three leading inference systems DeepSpeed Zero-Inference, Hugging Face Accelerate, and FlexGen by up to 29x, 29x, and 3x on OPT-6.7B and OPT-30B. With the same batch size, H2O can reduce the latency by up to 1.9x.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 4-5, Tables 1-2 (lm-eval-harness tasks, XSUM ROUGE, perplexity); 5-10x KV reduction at comparable accuracy
KV cache budget % (e.g. 20%); up to 5x footprint reduction

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The evaluation metric is generation throughput, which is the number of generated tokens / (prompt time + decoding time).
metric_definitions.notes: Output tokens only, per whole run of a fixed batch; denominator includes prefill (prompt) time and the time to construct the H2O KV cache; single GPU; throughput benefits come mostly from larger batch / avoiding offloading.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: All the speedup results are tested in an end-to-end setting, including both the pre-filling and generation phases. And it includes the time for constructing the H2O KV cache.
metric_definitions.locator: §5.2; Table 5 (latency in seconds for given prompt+generation length at a fixed batch size)
metric_definitions.notes: Latency = wall-clock time to finish a fixed batch of prompt+generation, not per-token or per-request; no queueing, no arrival process.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Table 5: Generation throughput and latency on an A100 GPU. In the sequence length row, we use "7000 + 1024" to denote a prompt length of 7000 and a generation length of 1024.
metric_definitions.notes: wall-clock time to generate a whole fixed batch (prompt+generation lengths, given batch size) offline; not TTFT/TPOT or per-request latency

load_regime: offline batch, synthetic prompts padded to equal length, fixed batch sizes; XSUM real dataset
tradeoff_acknowledged: Accuracy vs KV budget: comparable accuracy at <=20% budget; 'strided'/'fixed' sparse baselines fail at 20% budget; extreme budgets degrade.
hardware: NVIDIA T4 (16GB) with CPU offload; A100 80GB
workloads: lm-eval-harness/HELM tasks, XSUM, synthetic fixed-length prompts
extractor_notes: Algorithm optimizes KV cache size subject to accuracy (formulated as dynamic submodular eviction with an approximation guarantee); throughput is a systems consequence (bigger batch, no offload). Latency is whole-batch completion time, not TTFT/TPOT. No request-level SLO.
